The Grammar timetable follows a six day cycle, with the days labelled $A$ to $F$. In a certain year, the first school day is Monday and is an A day. Part of the timetable is shown in the table below, with weeks 8 to 35 omitted. For simplicity we assume the entire school year consists of 40 weeks.

parts.latex: Find the probability that a randomly selected school day is an A day.
When a school day is randomly selected, find the probability that the day is an A day, given that it is a Monday. Hence state, with justification, whether these two events are independent.

Suppose there are:

\begin{itemize}
\item $0$ periods of maths on A days.
\item $1$ period of maths on B days.
\item $2$ periods of maths on each of D, E and F days.
\item $3$ periods of maths on C days.
\end{itemize}

Let $X$ be the number of maths periods on a randomly chosen Monday. Find $E(X)$.

solutions.latex:
The six-day cycle runs across five-day weeks. There is an A day every week except weeks $6,12,18,24,30,36$, so $34$ A days in $200$ school days:
$$P(\text{A})=\dfrac{34}{200}=\dfrac{17}{100}=17\%$$

Of the $40$ Mondays, $7$ are A days:
$$P(\text{A}\,|\,\text{Monday})=\dfrac{|\text{A}\cap\text{Monday}|}{|\text{Mondays}|}=\dfrac{7}{40}=17.5\%$$
This is not equal to $P(\text{A})=17\%$ from part (a), so the events are not independent.

Day types on the $40$ Mondays:
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{A}\,|\,\text{Mon})&=P(\text{D}\,|\,\text{Mon})=P(\text{E}\,|\,\text{Mon})=P(\text{F}\,|\,\text{Mon})=\dfrac{7}{40} \\ P(\text{B}\,|\,\text{Mon})&=P(\text{C}\,|\,\text{Mon})=\dfrac{6}{40}=\dfrac{3}{20}=15\% \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} E(X)&=0\times\dfrac{7}{40}+1\times\dfrac{6}{40}+2\times\dfrac{7}{40}\times 3+3\times\dfrac{6}{40} \\ &=1.65 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct probabilities for each day type on a Monday, or equivalent merit

Using the quadratic formula on $2k^2-k+0.12=0$:

$$\therefore\ k=0.3$$

Expected values add over games, so for $3$ games the expected amount is $3E(X)$:
$$\begin{aligned} 3E(X) &= 3\times(-0.05) \\ &= -\$0.15 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{lose exactly twice}) &= 3\times(0.11)^2\times(1-0.11) \\ &= 0.032307 \\ &= 3.2307\% \end{aligned}$$
